page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.2-32 is a flexible compute instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor with an x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical processor cores at 2 threads per core, running at a clock frequency of 3.9 GHz. It features 32 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 8 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled, necessitating remote block storage attachments for persistent filesystem operations. In addition, the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

With an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is configured for memory-intensive requirements rather than heavily multithreaded compute. Dedicated core allocation guarantees consistent access to CPU execution cycles without noisy-neighbor contention from shared virtualization resources. Because the configuration carries a comparatively high RAM capacity relative to its 4 vCPUs, it delivers resource density for memory-bound applications without requiring overprovisioning of processor cores. The lack of integrated local NVMe storage means storage throughput and latency depend on the attached network block storage service.

The hardware profile suits memory-caching layers, small to mid-sized in-memory databases, transactional backend services, and application runtimes with significant memory working sets. It is also suitable for microservices, lightweight data transformation, and staging environments where RAM headroom is critical but multi-core parallel computing is not a primary bottleneck.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard4.Ax.Flex.2-32 is a memory-oriented flexible compute instance designed around the Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor operating on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a sustained clock speed of 3.9 GHz. Accompanied by 32 GB of system memory, the instance establishes an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, offering substantial memory capacity for memory-bound tasks without requiring excess processor allocations. The server does not bundle local disk storage, relying instead on network block volumes for persistent data retention, and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated CPU allocation mitigating multi-tenant resource contention, the instance provides predictable execution for workloads sensitive to RAM capacity. It is well matched for mid-sized in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, enterprise application servers, lightweight analytics pipelines, and memory-heavy web microservices.
